title: Elliptic curves
covers: Point addition, doubling, ECC vs RSA key size
learningGoals: You will be able to explain the geometric equation y^2 = x^3 + ax + b of an elliptic curve.
You will be able to demonstrate point addition and point doubling geometrically.
You will be able to compare ECC 256-bit security against RSA 3072-bit key sizes.

lessonCards.title: The Elliptic Curve Equation
lessonCards.analogy: A smooth, symmetric roller-coaster loop shaped by the formula: y^2 = x^3 + ax + b.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Defined over prime fields F_p, an elliptic curve forms an abelian group with a special 'point at infinity' O acting as identity.
lessonCards.example: NIST curve P-256 and Bitcoin's secp256k1 are the most widely deployed curves on earth.

lessonCards.title: Point Addition & Point Doubling
lessonCards.analogy: Drawing a line through two points on the curve: it intersects a third point; reflect it across the x-axis to find P + Q.
lessonCards.coreConcept: If P != Q, draw the chord line to find intersection R, then reflect: P + Q = -R. If adding P to itself (point doubling P + P), draw the tangent line.
lessonCards.example: Repeating point addition k times computes public key Q = k * P using double-and-add.

lessonCards.title: Small Keys, Titanic Strength
lessonCards.analogy: A tiny diamond laser lock providing more protection than a massive 10-foot iron bank door.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Because there is no sub-exponential attack against the Elliptic Curve Discrete Log Problem (ECDLP), a 256-bit ECC key matches the strength of a huge 3072-bit RSA key.
lessonCards.example: Saves 90% bandwidth and battery power on smartphones, smart watches, and IoT sensors.

questions.prompt: What is the standard Weierstrass algebraic equation for an elliptic curve over a real field?
options: y^2 = x^3 + ax + b
y = mx + b
y = x^2
questions.explanation: The standard non-singular cubic equation is y^2 = x^3 + ax + b, where 4a^3 + 27b^2 != 0.
wrongExplanations: Correct! y^2 = x^3 + ax + b is the elliptic curve equation.
y = mx + b is a straight line.
x^2 + y^2 = r^2 is a circle.
y = x^2 is a simple parabola.
questions.realWorldExample: Neil Koblitz and Victor Miller independently proposed using elliptic curves for cryptography in 1985.

questions.prompt: How does a 256-bit Elliptic Curve key (e.g. NIST P-256) compare in cryptographic security to an RSA key?
options: A 256-bit ECC key offers equivalent security to an RSA 3072-bit key
A 256-bit ECC key is much weaker than RSA-512
RSA keys are always 100x stronger than any ECC key
They are identical in bit length and speed
questions.explanation: NIST guidelines equate 256-bit elliptic curves (128 bits of symmetric security) to a 3072-bit RSA key, with vastly smaller signature sizes and faster computation.
wrongExplanations: Correct! 256-bit ECC matches 3072-bit RSA.
256-bit ECC is orders of magnitude stronger than broken RSA-512.
ECC offers vastly superior security-per-bit than RSA.
RSA requires over 10x more bits.
questions.realWorldExample: Apple iMessage, WhatsApp, and TLS 1.3 default to elliptic curves to maximize battery life.

questions.prompt: In the geometric definition of point addition on an elliptic curve, how is P + Q determined?
options: Draw a straight line through P and Q, find the third intersection point on the curve, and reflect it across the x-axis
Add the x coordinates and multiply the y coordinates
Draw a circle around P and Q
Calculate the average of both coordinates
questions.explanation: A line intersecting points P and Q intersects the curve at a third point R; reflecting R across the x-axis (x, -y) gives P + Q.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Chord-and-tangent reflection defines group addition.
Coordinate addition is non-linear.
Circles do not define group laws.
Averages do not lie on the curve.
questions.realWorldExample: If P = Q, the tangent line at P is drawn (point doubling).

questions.prompt: What is the 'Point at Infinity' (O) in Elliptic Curve arithmetic?
options: The additive identity element of the group (equivalent to 0: P + O = P)
A point that crashes the computer
A point located at coordinates (9999, 9999)
A point outside the universe
questions.explanation: The point at infinity O acts as the identity element of the group, just like 0 in ordinary addition: P + (-P) = O.
wrongExplanations: Correct! The point at infinity is the group identity element.
It is cleanly handled by software as an identity flag.
It is an ideal geometric point, not a literal coordinate.
It is standard projective geometry.
questions.realWorldExample: Vertical lines intersect the curve at (x, y), (x, -y), and the point at infinity O.

questions.prompt: What is the hard mathematical problem that protects Elliptic Curve Cryptography?
options: The Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem (ECDLP)
Factoring two prime numbers
Sorting an array in O(1) time
Finding the perimeter of a rectangle
questions.explanation: Given curve points P and Q = k * P, finding the scalar integer k is the Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem (ECDLP).
wrongExplanations: Correct! Solving k in Q = k * P takes fully exponential Pollard's rho time O(sqrt(n)).
Factoring primes protects RSA, not ECC.
Array sorting is unrelated.
Perimeter calculation is elementary.
questions.realWorldExample: The best known classical attacks against ECDLP take exponential time, whereas RSA factoring takes sub-exponential time.

questions.prompt: Which popular cryptocurrency uses the Koblitz curve 'secp256k1' for public address generation and transaction signing?
options: Bitcoin
Visa Credit Card
PayPal
Fedwire
questions.explanation: Satoshi Nakamoto selected the secp256k1 curve (y^2 = x^3 + 7 mod p) for all Bitcoin ECDSA key pairs and digital signatures.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Bitcoin and Ethereum use secp256k1.
Visa utilizes EMV chip smart cards.
PayPal is a payment processor.
Fedwire is an interbank transfer network.
questions.realWorldExample: secp256k1 features efficient endomorphisms that allow faster point multiplication.

ashRecap: Elliptic curves give you bank-grade security with tiny 256-bit keys. Points bounce across the curve to create the world's most efficient crypto locks!
